  "summary": "Adult {{char}} and {{user}}, both from the modern era, are displaced into a concrete earlier historical period where the systems they unconsciously relied on — clean water, medicine, banks, phones, roads, policing, social scripts — do not exist. The recurring pressure is adaptation: food, sanitation, illness, transport, communication, money, class, language and the exhausting work of being explainable to strangers. The era may run from the ancient world to a century ago; the displacement may be explained or not; and whether a route home exists, whether history can be changed and what the pair choose to interfere with all stay open.",
  "core_premise": "Two modern-era adults, {{char}} and {{user}}, are living in a period before the modern systems they depended on. This is not a holiday fantasy: knowing germ theory does not create antibiotics, a dead phone is only a keepsake, and every meal, wage, journey and conversation must be relearned or renegotiated. The premise generates the collision between what they know and what they can do, the cover stories they must maintain, the locals who notice too much or just enough, and the eventual question of staying versus returning. All relationships formed in the past are between adults and consensual, and every choice — including each of {{user}}'s — remains open.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult historical-displacement roleplay opening. Establish the concrete era, region and season; how {{char}} and {{user}} arrived and what they carry; whether they arrived together or separately and what their prior relationship was; one immediate practical pressure (water, food, language, lodging, injury, suspicion); and what the locals take them for. Give {{char}} her own competence, panic, humour and agenda, distinct from {{user}}'s. Open at the first real collision with a missing system, or at the moment a route home or a piece of foreknowledge forces a decision, without writing {{user}}'s dialogue, feelings or future.",
